places.name: Ismarus
places.tradition: Thracian coast near Maroneia (Strabo 7 fr. 44; Barrington Atlas lists as unlocated)
places.note: City of the Cicones sacked by Odysseus's men on leaving Troy. Ancient tradition (Strabo 7 fr. 44) locates it near Maroneia on the Thracian coast.

places.name: Cape Malea
places.note: Southeastern promontory of the Peloponnese; the storm that rounds Odysseus off course begins here.

places.name: Cythera
places.note: Island south of the Peloponnese past which the north wind and current drive Odysseus's ships off course.

places.name: Land of the Lotus-eaters
places.tradition: Meninx/Djerba, Tunisia, called Lotophagitis in antiquity (Polybius ap. Pliny NH 5.41)
places.note: Coast where three of Odysseus's men eat the lotus and lose all wish to return home. Ancient tradition (Polybius, Pliny NH 5.41) locates it at Meninx/Djerba off Tunisia.

places.name: Land of the Cyclopes
places.tradition: Sicily, near Mount Etna (Thucydides 6.2.1; Euripides' Cyclops)
places.note: Land of the lawless, one-eyed Cyclopes where Polyphemus blinds and imprisons Odysseus's crew. Ancient tradition (Thucydides 6.2.1) locates the Cyclopes in Sicily.

places.name: Aeolia
places.tradition: Aeolian/Lipari Islands off Sicily (Thucydides 3.88)
places.note: Floating island home of Aeolus, keeper of the winds, who gives Odysseus the bag of storm-winds. Ancient tradition (Thucydides 3.88) identifies it with the Aeolian (Lipari) Islands.

places.name: Laestrygonia (Telepylus)
places.tradition: Formiae, Italy (Roman literary tradition, Horace Odes 3.17; Homer's own text suggests a near-polar 'land of the long day', Od. 10.82-86)
places.note: Harbor city of the cannibal Laestrygonians, where all of Odysseus's ships but one are destroyed. Roman tradition (Horace, Odes 3.17) places it at Formiae, Italy.

places.name: Aeaea
places.tradition: Monte Circeo (ancient Circeii), Italy (Theophrastus HP 5.8.3; Roman literary tradition)
places.note: Island of the enchantress Circe, who transforms Odysseus's men into swine. Roman-era tradition (Theophrastus HP 5.8.3; later Latin poets) locates it at Monte Circeo on the Italian coast.

places.name: Land of the Cimmerians / entrance to the underworld
places.note: Sunless land at the edge of Ocean where Odysseus performs the nekyia. Homer gives no real-world geography; no ancient tradition fixes a location.

places.name: Island of the Sirens
places.tradition: Sirenusas (Li Galli islands) off Sorrento, Italy (Strabo 1.2.12, 5.4.8)
places.note: Unnamed island where the Sirens' song lures sailors to death; Odysseus sails past bound to the mast. Strabo (1.2.12, 5.4.8) locates it off the Sirenusas near Sorrento.

places.name: Planctae (Wandering Rocks)
places.note: Colliding rocks that only the Argo has ever passed safely; Circe advises Odysseus to avoid them for Scylla's strait instead. Ancient scholiasts disagreed on location, some conflating them with the Symplegades.

places.name: Scylla's rock
places.tradition: Strait of Messina, Italian shore (Thucydides 4.24.5)
places.note: Six-headed monster inhabiting a cliff opposite Charybdis, who seizes six of Odysseus's men. Thucydides (4.24.5) identifies the strait as the Strait of Messina.

places.name: Charybdis
places.tradition: Strait of Messina, Sicilian shore (Thucydides 4.24.5)
places.note: Whirlpool opposite Scylla that swallows the sea three times a day. Thucydides (4.24.5) identifies the strait as the Strait of Messina.

places.name: Thrinacia
places.tradition: Sicily, whose ancient name Trinacria echoes Thrinacia (Thucydides 6.2.2)
places.note: Island of the Sun-god's cattle; the crew's slaughter of the sacred herd dooms them. Thucydides (6.2.2) connects the name to Sicily (Trinacria).

places.name: Ogygia
places.note: Remote island of the nymph Calypso, where Odysseus is detained seven years. No ancient source offers a real-world identification commanding consensus; kept unlocated.

places.name: Scheria (Phaeacia)
places.tradition: Corcyra (modern Corfu), ancient tradition since Thucydides 1.25
places.note: Island home of the seafaring Phaeacians, who ferry Odysseus to Ithaca. Ancient tradition, beginning with Thucydides (1.25), identifies it with Corcyra (Corfu).

places.name: Egypt
places.note: Land and river of the Nile; destination of Menelaus's wandering and of Odysseus's Cretan false tales.

places.name: Pharos
places.note: Island off the Egyptian coast where Menelaus, becalmed, ambushes Proteus for sailing directions home.

places.name: Cyprus
places.note: Island named among the far shores of Menelaus's wandering and, elsewhere, as Aphrodite's own.

places.name: Sidon / Phoenicia
places.note: Phoenician city and coast; source of the traders and the ornate silver bowl given to Menelaus.

places.name: Libya
places.note: North African coast west of Egypt, named among the wonder-lands of Menelaus's wandering and Odysseus's false tales.

places.name: Thesprotia
places.note: Region of Epirus on the mainland; setting of several of Odysseus's false tales and home to King Pheidon.

places.name: Dodona
places.note: Oracular sanctuary of Zeus in Epirus, consulted in Odysseus's false tale to learn whether to return openly or in secret.

places.name: Land of the Ethiopians
places.note: Distant people 'sundered in twain' at the world's edge whom Poseidon visits at the poem's opening. Homer's own geography is schematic, not a fixed real-world location.

places.name: Troy (Ilios)
places.note: The besieged city; identified since Schliemann's 1870s excavations with the mound of Hisarlik in northwest Turkey.

places.name: Scamander (Xanthus)
places.note: Principal river of the Trojan plain, called Xanthus by the gods; its god fights Achilles in Iliad 21. Modern Karamenderes.

places.name: Simoeis
places.note: Tributary stream of the Scamander crossing the Trojan plain, paired with it as a boundary marker.

places.name: Mount Ida
places.note: Mountain range south of Troy where Zeus watches the war and to which Paris's judgment is traditionally set; modern Kaz Dağı.

places.name: Tenedos
places.note: Small island off the Trojan coast where the Achaean fleet hides to fake a withdrawal.

places.name: Imbros
places.note: Island near the Hellespont mouth, a waystation for gods travelling between Troy and Samothrace.

places.name: Samothrace
places.note: Northern Aegean island whose peak gives Poseidon a full view of the Trojan plain.

places.name: Lemnos
places.note: Aegean island where Hephaestus fell after being cast from Olympus; also the market for wine shipped to the Achaean camp and where Achilles sold Lycaon.

places.name: Chryse
places.tradition: Near Hamaxitos/Smintheion, Troad (Strabo 13.1.48, who reports the town already gone by his day)
places.note: Coastal town of the priest Chryses, sacred to Apollo Smintheus. Site disputed; Strabo (13.1.48) already found it vanished, tentatively placed near Hamaxitos.

places.name: Cilla
places.tradition: Troad, near Thebe under Placus (Strabo 13.1.62, site disputed and unlocated)
places.note: Town sacred to Apollo paired with Chryse in the priest's prayer; exact site unrecovered.

places.name: Thebe (under Placus)
places.tradition: Near Adramyttium (modern Edremit), Troad (Strabo 13.1.65-70)
places.note: Andromache's home city, sacked by Achilles, who kills her father Eetion. Strabo (13.1.65-70) places it near Adramyttium (modern Edremit).

places.name: Lyrnessus
places.tradition: Troad, exact site disputed already in antiquity (Strabo 13.1.60-70)
places.note: City sacked by Achilles where Briseis was captured; Strabo himself calls the site's identification uncertain.

places.name: Pedasus (Troad)
places.tradition: On the Satnioeis river, Troad, site unrecovered (Strabo 13.1.51)
places.note: Town on the Satnioeis river sacked with Lyrnessus; not securely located by modern archaeology.

places.name: Abydos
places.note: City on the Asian shore of the Hellespont, the narrowest crossing point; home of Trojan allies under Asius.

places.name: Sestos
places.note: City on the European shore of the Hellespont opposite Abydos.

places.name: Hellespont
places.note: Strait (modern Dardanelles) bounding the Troad, repeatedly named as the edge of the Achaeans' world.

places.name: Batieia
places.note: A mound before Troy that men call Batieia but the gods call the barrow of swift Myrina (Iliad 2.811-814); a real narrated landmark within the story, not merely mythical, but its physical site is not securely identified.
places.tradition: A tumulus on the Trojan plain, one of several (with the tombs of Ilus and Aesyetes) discussed in Troad topography since Strabo (13.1.36-37); no ancient or modern survey (e.g. Leaf, Troy: A Study in Homeric Geography, 1912) securely matches a surviving mound to Batieia.

places.name: Callicolone
places.tradition: Ridge east of Troy near the Simoeis (J. M. Cook, The Troad, 1973, tentative)
places.note: 'Fair hill' near the Simoeis where gods sit to watch the battle of the gods. Modern topographers (J. M. Cook, The Troad, 1973) propose a ridge east of Troy without certainty.

places.name: Thymbra
places.tradition: Confluence of the Thymbrios and Scamander rivers (Strabo 13.1.35)
places.note: District where the Trojans' Lycian and Mysian allies are posted; site of the later Thymbraion temple of Apollo. Strabo (13.1.35) places it at the Thymbrios-Scamander confluence.

places.name: Dardania
places.tradition: Near modern Çanakkale, south of Abydos (Strabo 13.1.25-33)
places.note: City founded by Dardanus before Ilios itself existed on the plain; ancient tradition places it near modern Çanakkale, south of Abydos.

places.name: Zeleia
places.tradition: Aesepus valley, near modern Sarıköy (Strabo 13.1.9)
places.note: City under the foot of Ida on the Aesepus, home of Pandarus and his Trojan-allied archers. Strabo places it near the Aesepus valley.

places.name: The washing-troughs
places.tradition: Beside Troy/Hisarlik, following the certain city identification
places.note: Twin springs, one hot and one cold, beside the road from Troy where Achilles runs down Hector; a fixture of the Trojan plain in the certain Hisarlik identification.

places.name: Phthia
places.tradition: Spercheios river valley, Thessaly, near ancient Halos/Pharsalus (disputed; Strabo 9.5.6)
places.note: Achilles' homeland in Thessaly, whose exact site (Spercheios valley, near Pharsalus/Halos) is disputed among ancient and modern geographers.

places.name: Mycenae
places.note: Agamemnon's citadel, the wealthiest of the Achaean cities; identified with the Bronze Age site excavated by Schliemann from 1874.

places.name: Argos
places.note: City of the Argolid; Homer also uses 'Argos' loosely for the wider Peloponnese/Achaea, a usage noted since antiquity.

places.name: Salamis
places.note: Island home of Telamonian Ajax, named in his own prayer before facing Hector in single combat.

places.name: Locris
places.note: Homeland of the Locrians under the lesser Ajax, on the Greek mainland opposite Euboea.

places.name: Euboea
places.note: Long island off the eastern coast of central Greece; Nestor's route home runs past it via the open sea crossing.

places.name: Calydon
places.note: Aetolian city at the center of the Meleager story told by Phoenix in his appeal to Achilles.

places.name: Aetolia
places.note: Region of west-central Greece around Calydon; named as the homeland of the man who tricks Eumaeus's false Cretan into a lie about Odysseus.

places.name: Same
places.note: One of the islands in Odysseus's kingdom, alongside Ithaca, Dulichium, and Zacynthus (Odyssey 1.246, 9.24). The Iliad's Catalogue of Ships names it in the older form Σάμος (2.634); identified with modern Kefalonia.
places.tradition: Identified with the island now called Cephalonia (Kefalonia), whose principal town Sami preserves the ancient name. In Homer 'Same' names one island in Odysseus's realm; it is distinct from 'Cephallenians' (Κεφαλλῆνες, Iliad 2.631), the ethnonym covering Odysseus's whole people across Ithaca, Same, Dulichium, Zacynthus, and the mainland opposite.

places.name: Zacynthus
places.note: Wooded island in Odysseus's kingdom, south of Cephallenia; modern Zakynthos.

places.name: Dulichium
places.tradition: Possibly the Echinades group or an island near Cephallenia; disputed since antiquity (Strabo 10.2.19)
places.note: Fourth island of Odysseus's realm, supplying the largest single contingent of suitors. Its identity was already disputed in antiquity.

places.name: Athens
places.note: City of Attica, Athena's own city, visited by the goddess herself in the Odyssey.

places.name: Elis
places.note: Region of the northwest Peloponnese, home of the Epeans, named in Nestor's account of a cattle-raid.

places.name: Orchomenus (Minyan)
places.note: Wealthy Boeotian city, invoked by Achilles as a byword for riches he will refuse from Agamemnon.

places.name: Thebes (Boeotia)
places.note: Seven-gated Boeotian city captured by the Epigoni; distinct from the Cilician Thebe of the Troad.

places.name: Aulis
places.note: Boeotian harbor where the Achaean fleet gathered before Troy; site of the portent Odysseus recalls.

places.name: Delphi (Pytho)
places.note: Sanctuary of Apollo at the foot of Parnassus, named for its treasuries in both epics.

places.name: Ithaca
places.note: Odysseus's home island, ruled by continuity of name with the modern island of Ithaki since antiquity (Strabo 10.2.10-13).
places.tradition: Identified since antiquity with the island of Ithaki (Strabo 10.2.10-13). A minority 'Paliki thesis' (Bittlestone, Diggle & Underhill, Odysseus Unbound, 2005) argues Homer's Ithaca is instead the Paliki peninsula of Kefalonia, once a separate island; the Ithaki identification remains the mainstream tradition.

places.name: Pylos
places.tradition: Ano Englianos, Messenia (Blegen's excavations from 1939, identifying the 'Palace of Nestor')
places.note: Nestor's 'sandy Pylos' in Messenia, identified by most archaeologists with the excavated Bronze Age palace at Ano Englianos (Blegen, from 1939).

places.name: Sparta (Lacedaemon)
places.note: Menelaus and Helen's home in Laconia, Telemachus's second stop on his journey for news of his father.

places.name: Crete (Cnossus)
places.note: Idomeneus's kingdom and, in the Odyssey, Cnossus is named as Minos's great city; also the setting of Odysseus's recurring false Cretan identity.

places.name: Hyria
places.note: Coastal town opposite Aulis in Strabo's account; no firm modern site identified.
places.tradition: Coastal Boeotia opposite Aulis (Strabo 9.2.12); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Schoenus
places.note: Boeotian village on the Theban-Anthedon road per Strabo; site not confirmed archaeologically.
places.tradition: Near Thebes on the road to Anthedon (Strabo 9.2.24); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Scolus
places.note: Village below Cithaeron that Strabo calls a rough, hardly livable place; unlocated precisely.
places.tradition: Foothills of Cithaeron near Thebes (Strabo 9.2.23; Paus. 9.4.4); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Eteonus
places.note: "Many-ridged" Boeotian village; Strabo says it was later called Scarphe. Site unconfirmed.
places.tradition: Cithaeron foothills, later renamed Scarphe per Strabo 9.2.25; Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Thespiae
places.note: Boeotian city under Mt Helicon; modern Thespies preserves the name over the excavated remains.
places.tradition: Identified with the excavated site near modern Thespies/Erimokastro, Boeotia (Paus. 9.26)

places.name: Graea
places.note: Strabo equates Graea with Tanagra, but the identification is his own inference, not certain.
places.tradition: Possibly Tanagra or Oropus area, East Boeotia (Strabo 9.2.6, identifies it with Tanagra); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Mycalessus
places.note: "Wide-lawned" Boeotian town on the road to Chalcis; the Thucydidean massacre site near Ritsona.
places.tradition: Near modern Ritsona, East Boeotia (site of the Thucydides 7.29 massacre; Paus. 9.19.4)

places.name: Harma
places.note: Village near Mycalessus and Tanagra; Strabo links its name to Amphiaraus's chariot. Unconfirmed site.
places.tradition: Near modern Kastro, East Boeotia, associated with lightning omens (Strabo 9.2.11); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Eilesium
places.note: Minor Boeotian village grouped with Harma and Erythrae; no confirmed modern site.
places.tradition: East Boeotia, exact site unknown; Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Erythrae (Boeotia)
places.note: Boeotian village distinct from Ionian Erythrae; no confirmed modern site.
places.tradition: East Boeotia, near Mycalessus; Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Eleon
places.note: Boeotian town excavated since 2011 by the Eastern Boeotia Archaeological Project near modern Arma.
places.tradition: Excavated at the site called Ancient Eleon near modern Arma/Dritsa, East Boeotia (excavations from 2011)

places.name: Hyle
places.note: Village by the lake Strabo calls Hylica (a Copais inlet); precise site unconfirmed.
places.tradition: Shore of Lake Copais/Hylica, Boeotia (Strabo 9.2.20); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Peteon
places.note: Minor Boeotian village; Strabo places it on the road from Thebes toward the coast.
places.tradition: Between Thebes and the coast, Boeotia (Strabo 9.2.28); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Ocalea
places.note: Village Strabo places on the road between Haliartus and Alalcomenae; site unconfirmed.
places.tradition: Midway between Haliartus and Alalcomenae, Boeotia (Strabo 9.2.27); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Medeon (Boeotia)
places.note: Boeotian coastal town, distinct from Phocian Medeon; excavated remains near modern Kastraki.
places.tradition: Identified with the excavated site near modern Kastraki on the Gulf of Corinth (Boeotian Medeon)

places.name: Copae
places.note: Lake-shore town giving Copais its name; site at modern Kastro on the drained lake's edge.
places.tradition: Identified with the site at modern Kastro/Topolia on the former Lake Copais shore

places.name: Eutresis
places.note: Boeotian village excavated by Hetty Goldman (1924-27) near modern Leuktra; continuous Bronze Age habitation.
places.tradition: Excavated Bronze Age site near modern Leuktra, Boeotia (Goldman excavations, 1924-1927)

places.name: Thisbe
places.note: "Many-doved" Boeotian town; modern Thisvi sits on/near the ancient site below Mt Helicon.
places.tradition: Modern village of Thisvi, Boeotia, preserves the ancient name (Paus. 9.32.2-3)

places.name: Coroneia
places.note: Site of the federal Boeotian sanctuary of Athena Itonia; modern Koroneia preserves the name.
places.tradition: Modern village of Koroneia, Boeotia, on the site of the ancient city (Paus. 9.34)

places.name: Haliartus
places.note: Boeotian city on Lake Copais's south shore, destroyed 171 BC; modern Aliartos preserves the name.
places.tradition: Excavated site near modern Aliartos, Boeotia (Paus. 9.33)

places.name: Plataea
places.note: Boeotian city of the 479 BC battle; modern Plataies preserves the name over the excavated remains.
places.tradition: Excavated site near modern Plataies, Boeotia, below Mt Cithaeron (Paus. 9.1-4)

places.name: Glisas
places.note: Village near Teumessus at the foot of Mt Hypatus per Strabo/Pausanias; precise site unconfirmed.
places.tradition: Foot of Mt Hypatus, East Boeotia (Strabo 9.2.34; Paus. 9.19.3); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Hypothebae
places.note: "Lower Thebes": the Catalogue names this, not ruined Thebes itself, per the tradition that the Epigoni sacked Thebes one generation before Troy.
places.tradition: The Theban settlement re-founded after the Epigoni destroyed seven-gated Thebes (schol. Il. 2.505; Paus. 9.8.4-9.5)

places.name: Onchestus
places.note: Grove and sanctuary of Poseidon on the road from Haliartus to Thebes, still visible in antiquity.
places.tradition: Sanctuary of Poseidon located near modern Steni/Haliartos, Boeotia (Paus. 9.26.5; Strabo 9.2.33)

places.name: Arne
places.note: Boeotian city Strabo says may have been swallowed by Lake Copais; identification disputed since antiquity.
places.tradition: Possibly submerged under Lake Copais or identified with Acraephnium (Strabo 9.2.34-35); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Midea (Boeotia)
places.note: Boeotian town distinct from Argive Midea; Strabo places it near Lake Copais without precision.
places.tradition: Copaic basin, Boeotia, exact site unknown (Strabo 9.2.35); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Nisa
places.note: Strabo himself questions whether a Boeotian Nisa existed, suggesting the line may name Isus instead.
places.tradition: Site disputed; Strabo doubts a Boeotian Nisa existed and proposes emending the text (Strabo 9.2.14); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Anthedon
places.note: "Farthest-lying" Boeotian coastal town facing Euboea; site located near modern Loukisia.
places.tradition: Coastal site near modern Loukisia, East Boeotia (Strabo 9.2.13; Paus. 9.22.5)

places.name: Aspledon
places.note: Minyan town paired with Orchomenus; Strabo places it a short distance north of Orchomenus.
places.tradition: Near modern Pyrgos, north of Orchomenus, Boeotia (Strabo 9.2.26)

places.name: Cyparissus (Phocis)
places.note: Phocian town near Delphi; Strabo connects the name to later Anticyra on the Corinthian Gulf.
places.tradition: Identified with Anticyra or its vicinity on the Corinthian Gulf, Phocis (Strabo 9.3.13)

places.name: Crisa
places.note: City on the height above the Crisaean/Cirrhaean plain, the harbor-district of Delphi.
places.tradition: Excavated site above the Crisaean plain near Delphi, Phocis (Strabo 9.3.3)

places.name: Daulis
places.note: Phocian city of the Procne/Philomela myth; modern Davleia preserves the name over the ancient site.
places.tradition: Modern village of Davleia/Daulis, Phocis, on the ancient site (Paus. 10.4.7)

places.name: Panopeus
places.note: Small Phocian city on the border with Boeotia; Pausanias describes its walls as still standing.
places.tradition: Excavated walls near modern Agios Vlasios, Phocis (Paus. 10.4.1-4)

places.name: Anemoreia
places.note: "Windy" Phocian settlement Strabo says was later renamed Anemolea; precise site unconfirmed.
places.tradition: Windy pass site near Delphi, later called Anemolea per Strabo 9.3.15; Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Hyampolis
places.note: Northeast Phocian town near the excavated Kalapodi sanctuary; site attested by Pausanias.
places.tradition: Near modern Exarchos/Kalapodi, Phocis (Paus. 10.35.5; excavations at the Kalapodi sanctuary)

places.name: Cephisus (river)
places.note: River draining Phocis into the Copaic basin of Boeotia; the modern Kifisos still bears the name.

places.name: Lilaea
places.note: Town at the Cephisus's source on Parnassus; modern Lilaia preserves the ancient name and site.
places.tradition: Modern village of Lilaia, Phocis, at the springs of the Cephisus on Mt Parnassus (Paus. 10.33.4)

places.name: Cynus
places.note: Harbor-town of Opus on the Euboean Gulf; located near modern Livanates.
places.tradition: Port of Opus near modern Livanates, East Locris (Strabo 9.4.2)

places.name: Opus
places.note: Chief city of the Opuntian Locrians and, in tradition, Patroclus's birthplace.
places.tradition: Modern town of Atalanti area, East Locris, capital of the Opuntian Locrians (Strabo 9.4.2)

places.name: Calliarus
places.note: Locrian town Strabo says had vanished by his own day; no confirmed site.
places.tradition: East Locris, exact site unknown; already lost by Strabo's time (Strabo 9.4.5); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Bessa
places.note: "Wooded glen" Locrian town, likewise vanished by antiquity per Strabo; unlocated.
places.tradition: East Locris, exact site unknown; also lost by Strabo's time (Strabo 9.4.5); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Scarphe
places.note: East Locrian coastal town on the road to Thermopylae, near modern Molos.
places.tradition: Near modern Molos, East Locris, on the coast road (Strabo 9.4.6)

places.name: Augeiae (Locris)
places.note: Locrian town of the same name as one in Laconia; vanished by Strabo's day, unlocated.
places.tradition: East Locris, exact site unknown, distinct from the Laconian Augeiae; already lost by Strabo's time (9.4.5); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Tarphe
places.note: Wooded Locrian town, later called Pharygae per Strabo, near the modern Kalapodi sanctuary area.
places.tradition: Later renamed Pharygae, near modern Kalapodi/Mendenitsa, East Locris (Strabo 9.4.6)

places.name: Thronium
places.note: Locrian town on the Boagrius river's banks, capital-adjacent to Thermopylae's approach.
places.tradition: Near modern Kainourgio/Pikraki, East Locris, on the Boagrius (Strabo 9.4.4)

places.name: Boagrius (river)
places.note: Torrent-river at Thronium in East Locris; Strabo notes it also went by the name Manes.
places.tradition: The stream by Thronium, East Locris, called Manes/Boagrius in antiquity (Strabo 9.4.4)

places.name: Chalcis (Euboea)
places.note: Chief city of Euboea on the Euripus strait; modern Chalkida occupies the same site.

places.name: Eretria
places.note: Excavated Euboean city (Homeric "Eiretria"); modern Eretria sits on the ancient site.

places.name: Histiaea
places.note: North Euboean city; classical Histiaea/Oreus is generally located near modern Oreoi.
places.tradition: North Euboea, near modern Oreoi (Strabo 10.1.3-4)

places.name: Cerinthus
places.note: Small coastal Euboean town on the Aegean side, near modern Mantoudi/Kerinthos.
places.tradition: Coastal North Euboea near modern Mantoudi (Strabo 10.1.3)

places.name: Dium (Euboea)
places.note: "Steep" Euboean town near Cape Cenaeum at the island's northwest tip; precise site unconfirmed.
places.tradition: North Euboea near Cape Cenaeum, exact site unknown; Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Carystus
places.note: South Euboean city famed for its marble quarries; modern Karystos occupies the ancient site.

places.name: Styra
places.note: South Euboean town between Carystus and Eretria; modern Nea Styra preserves the name nearby.
places.tradition: South Euboea near modern Nea Styra (Strabo 10.1.6)

places.name: Tiryns
places.note: Bronze Age citadel of the Argolid, famed for its Cyclopean walls; excavated by Schliemann from 1884.

places.name: Hermione
places.note: Argolid coastal city; modern Ermioni occupies the ancient site on its own peninsula.

places.name: Asine
places.note: Excavated Argolid coastal town near modern Tolo/Asini; Swedish excavations from 1922.

places.name: Troezen
places.note: Argolid city, Theseus's traditional birthplace; modern Troizina preserves the name.

places.name: Eionae
places.note: Small Argolid port Strabo says was later abandoned, its people moving to Argos; unlocated precisely.
places.tradition: Argolid coast near Epidaurus, exact site unknown (Strabo 8.6.14); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Epidaurus
places.note: Argolid city famed for the sanctuary of Asclepius; modern Palaia Epidavros occupies the ancient site.

places.name: Aegina
places.note: Saronic Gulf island-city; modern Aegina preserves the name over the ancient site.

places.name: Mases
places.note: Small Argolid port Strabo says was a dependency of Hermione by his own time; unlocated precisely.
places.tradition: Argolid coast near Hermione, already absorbed by Hermione in Strabo's day (Strabo 8.6.15); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Corinth
places.note: Isthmus city commanding two seas; the classical/Roman site underlies modern ancient Corinth.

places.name: Cleonae
places.note: Argolid city between Corinth and Argos; site excavated near modern Archaies Kleones.

places.name: Orneiae
places.note: Argolid town between Sicyon and Phlius; Strabo notes it later stood deserted.
places.tradition: Between Sicyon and Argos, Argolid, near modern Sterna/Kaparelli (Strabo 8.6.24)

places.name: Araethyrea
places.note: "Lovely" district Strabo identifies with the later city of Phlius; precise Homeric-era site unconfirmed.
places.tradition: Sicyonian territory, later called Phlius per Strabo 8.6.24; Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Sicyon
places.note: City of the Corinthian Gulf coast, Adrastus's first kingdom per Homer; excavated near modern Vasiliko.

places.name: Hyperesia
places.note: Achaean coastal town, later renamed Aegira; site near modern Aigeira on the Gulf of Corinth.
places.tradition: Later renamed Aegira, on the Corinthian Gulf, Achaea (Strabo 8.7.5; Paus. 7.26.1)

places.name: Gonoessa
places.note: "Steep" Achaean town Strabo could not securely place; sometimes emended to Donoessa.
places.tradition: Achaean coast near Aegira, exact site unknown; possibly = Donoessa (Strabo 8.7.5); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Pellene
places.note: Easternmost of the twelve Achaean cities; site near modern Pellini, above Xylokastro.
places.tradition: Achaean city near modern Pellini/Zougra (Strabo 8.7.5; Paus. 7.26-27)

places.name: Aegium
places.note: Chief city of Achaea, meeting-place of the Achaean League; modern Aigio occupies the ancient site.

places.name: Aegialus (Achaea)
places.note: "The coastland": Homer's name for the whole Corinthian Gulf shore later called Achaea.

places.name: Helice
places.note: Achaean city submerged by earthquake/tsunami in 373 BC; site located offshore near modern Rodia/Elike.

places.name: Pharis
places.note: Laconian town Strabo groups with Amyclae as later absorbed into Sparta's territory; unlocated precisely.
places.tradition: Laconia, near Amyclae, exact site unknown (Strabo 8.5.3); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Messe
places.note: "Many-doved" Laconian town Strabo could not confidently locate; possibly related to Messa on the gulf.
places.tradition: Laconia, possibly = later Messa on the Messenian Gulf (Strabo 8.5.3); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Bryseiae
places.note: Minor Laconian town paired with Augeiae in the Catalogue; no confirmed site.
places.tradition: Laconia, exact site unknown; Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Augeiae (Laconia)
places.note: Laconian town of the same name as one in East Locris; unlocated.
places.tradition: Laconia, exact site unknown, distinct from the Locrian Augeiae; Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Amyclae
places.note: Excavated sanctuary of Apollo south of Sparta; the pre-Dorian settlement absorbed into Lacedaemon.

places.name: Helos (Laconia)
places.note: Coastal marsh-town at the Eurotas's mouth; ancient tradition derives 'helot' from its conquest.
places.tradition: Marsh town near the Eurotas mouth, Laconia, later giving 'helot' its name (Strabo 8.5.4; Paus. 3.20.6)

places.name: Laas
places.note: Laconian town on the Mani coast; Pausanias locates its ruins near a hill by the same name.
places.tradition: South Laconia near modern Passava/Kyparissos (Paus. 3.24.6-8)

places.name: Oetylus
places.note: Mani-coast Laconian town; modern Oitylo preserves the ancient name on the same site.

places.name: Arene
places.note: Town Strabo could not confidently place, near the Minyeius in Triphylia; disputed since antiquity.
places.tradition: Messenia/Triphylia, near the Minyeius river, exact site disputed (Strabo 8.3.19); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Thryum
places.note: Named as "the ford of Alpheius"; Strabo locates it in Triphylia near the river crossing.
places.tradition: The ford of the Alpheius in Triphylia, near modern Epitalio (Strabo 8.3.13)

places.name: Aipy
places.note: "Steep" town in Triphylian territory; Strabo notes only the descriptive name, not a firm site.
places.tradition: Triphylia, 'the steep town,' exact site unknown (Strabo 8.3.24); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Cyparisseeis
places.note: Messenian coastal town; modern Kyparissia preserves the ancient name in the same region.
places.tradition: Near modern Kyparissia, Messenia (Strabo 8.3.24-25)

places.name: Amphigeneia
places.note: Triphylian town with a sanctuary of Leto per Strabo; precise site unconfirmed.
places.tradition: Triphylia, near the Hypsoeis river, exact site unknown (Strabo 8.3.25); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Pteleos (Messenia)
places.note: Messenian-area town, homonymous with a Thessalian town in the same Catalogue; unlocated.
places.tradition: Triphylia/Messenia, exact site unknown, distinct from the Thessalian Pteleos (Strabo 8.3.25); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Helos (Messenia)
places.note: Messenian coastal town sharing its name with the Laconian Helos in the same Catalogue; unlocated.
places.tradition: Messenia, exact site unknown, distinct from the Laconian Helos; Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Dorium
places.note: Site where the Muses blinded Thamyris; often linked with the Bronze Age site of Malthi in Messenia.
places.tradition: Messenia/Triphylia, site of the Thamyris myth, near modern Malthi (Strabo 8.3.25; Paus. 4.33.3)

places.name: Oechalia
places.note: Eurytus's city; already in antiquity Strabo lists rival Thessalian, Messenian, and Euboean claimants to the name.
places.tradition: Named at Il. 2.596 (Messenia, home of Eurytus) and 2.730 (Thessaly); ancient sources dispute whether one or several places bore the name (Strabo 9.5.17; 10.1.10); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Mount Cyllene
places.note: Highest mountain in the Peloponnese, birthplace of Hermes; modern Mt Ziria/Kyllini.

places.name: Tomb of Aepytus
places.note: Landmark tomb of the legendary Arcadian king Aepytus; Pausanias reports a real tumulus was pointed out near Heraea.
places.tradition: A tumulus near Heraea, Arcadia, was shown as Aepytus's tomb in antiquity (Paus. 8.16.3)

places.name: Pheneus
places.note: Northern Arcadian city in its own mountain basin; excavated site near modern Fonia/Pheneos.

places.name: Orchomenus (Arcadia)
places.note: "Sheep-rich" Arcadian city, distinct from the Boeotian Orchomenus in the same Catalogue; excavated near modern Kalpaki.

places.name: Rhipe
places.note: Strabo explicitly says these three towns, and their location, could not be found even in his day.
places.tradition: One of a trio of Arcadian names (with Stratie, Enispe) already unlocatable to ancient scholars (Strabo 8.8.2); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Stratie
places.note: Paired with Rhipe and Enispe as a byword for an untraceable Homeric place already in antiquity.
places.tradition: Unlocated Arcadian town, grouped with Rhipe and Enispe by ancient scholars (Strabo 8.8.2); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Enispe
places.note: "Windy Enispe" became the ancient scholiasts' stock example of a Homeric place no one could locate.
places.tradition: 'Windy Enispe': proverbial in antiquity for an unfindable place (Strabo 8.8.2); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Tegea
places.note: Major southeast Arcadian city; excavated sanctuary of Athena Alea near modern Tegea village.

places.name: Mantinea
places.note: Central Arcadian city, site of major classical battles; excavated remains near modern Mantineia.

places.name: Stymphalus
places.note: Northeast Arcadian city by its namesake lake, home of the mythical Stymphalian birds; excavated site survives.

places.name: Parrhasia
places.note: District/town-group of southwest Arcadia, later absorbed into the synoecism of Megalopolis.
places.tradition: Southwest Arcadian district around modern Megalopolis basin (Strabo 8.8.1)

places.name: Buprasium
places.note: District/town of northeast Elis bordering Achaea; already partly deserted by Strabo's time.
places.tradition: Northeast Elis, between the Larisus and the sea (Strabo 8.3.7)

places.name: Hyrmine
places.note: Elean coastal village Strabo says had disappeared, its name surviving in the nearby fort Hormina.
places.tradition: Elis coast, vanished village later refounded as the fort Hormina (Strabo 8.3.10); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Myrsinus
places.note: Elean coastal village on the road from Elis to Dyme, near a sacred myrtle grove per Strabo.
places.tradition: Elis coast near modern Agios Ilias, on the road to Dyme (Strabo 8.3.10)

places.name: Olenian Rock
places.note: Rock-landmark in Elis, not the Aetolian city of the same root name; Strabo notes the identity was disputed.
places.tradition: Elis, a rock landmark of disputed location, distinct from Aetolian Olenus (Strabo 8.3.10); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Alesium
places.note: Elean landmark Strabo tentatively connects with a hill called Alesiaeum; unconfirmed.
places.tradition: Elis, possibly a hill near Amphidolis, exact site unknown (Strabo 8.3.10); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Echinades Islands
places.note: Small island group off the Acarnanian coast at the Achelous's mouth; modern Echinades retain the name.

places.name: Neritum
places.note: "Leaf-quivering" mountain of Ithaca named alongside the island itself; traditionally the island's main ridge.
places.tradition: Ithaca's principal mountain, traditionally Mt Neriton/Anogi (Strabo 10.2.10)

places.name: Crocyleia
places.note: Strabo himself calls this and Aegilips obscure places within Odysseus's realm; unlocated.
places.tradition: Cephallenian/Ithacan territory, exact site unknown (Strabo 10.2.10, calls it obscure); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Aegilips
places.note: "Rugged" place in Odysseus's kingdom that Strabo could not identify with confidence.
places.tradition: Cephallenian/Ithacan territory, exact site unknown (Strabo 10.2.10); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Pleuron
places.note: Aetolian city of the Meleager saga; the Classical-era city was refounded near the original Homeric site.
places.tradition: Old Pleuron near modern Gyphtokastro, Aetolia; refounded nearby after the Homeric site's destruction (Strabo 10.2.4)

places.name: Olenus (Aetolia)
places.note: Aetolian city Strabo reports as already razed and its territory absorbed by neighbors; unlocated.
places.tradition: Aetolia, already destroyed and deserted by Strabo's time (Strabo 10.2.6); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Pylene
places.note: Aetolian town Strabo says was moved to higher ground and renamed Proschium; original site unlocated.
places.tradition: Aetolia, relocated and renamed Proschium per Strabo 10.2.6; Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Chalcis (Aetolia)
places.note: Aetolian coastal town on the gulf, distinct from Euboean Chalcis named in the same Catalogue.
places.tradition: Aetolian coastal town near modern Vasiliki, homonymous with Euboean Chalcis (Strabo 10.2.4)

places.name: Gortyn
places.note: Major Cretan city, later Roman provincial capital; extensively excavated site survives near modern Gortyna.

places.name: Lyctus
places.note: Old Cretan city, a Spartan colony per tradition; modern Lyttos village preserves the name nearby.
places.tradition: East-central Crete near modern Xidas/Lyttos village (Strabo 10.4.14)

places.name: Miletus (Crete)
places.note: Cretan city sharing its name with Anatolian Miletus named later in this Catalogue's Trojan half.
places.tradition: South-central Crete, near modern Miletos village, homonymous with Anatolian Miletus (Strabo 10.4.14)

places.name: Lycastus
places.note: Cretan city Strabo lists among those absorbed by Cnossus or Gortyn well before his own day.
places.tradition: Crete, exact site unknown, already vanished by Strabo's time (Strabo 10.4.14); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Phaestus
places.note: Major Minoan palatial site in the Messara plain, south-central Crete; extensively excavated.

places.name: Rhytium
places.note: Small Cretan town Strabo lists as a dependency of Gortyn; near-namesake modern Rotasi village.
places.tradition: South-central Crete near modern Rotasi, subject to Gortyn (Strabo 10.4.14)

places.name: Crete
places.note: Large island south of the Aegean, called "hundred-citied" in this line; Idomeneus's and Minos's traditional realm.

places.name: Rhodes
places.note: Dodecanese island later unified from three cities (Lindus, Ialysus, Camirus); Tlepolemus's kingdom.

places.name: Lindus
places.note: East-coast Rhodian city with its acropolis sanctuary of Athena Lindia; modern Lindos occupies the site.

places.name: Ialysus
places.note: Northwest Rhodian city near modern Trianta/Ialysos; one of the island's three pre-synoecism cities.

places.name: Camirus
places.note: Excavated west-coast Rhodian city, one of the island's three pre-synoecism cities.

places.name: Ephyra
places.note: Astyocheia's city, captured by Heracles; Strabo catalogues rival Homeric Ephyras and cannot fix this one.
places.tradition: One of several Homeric Ephyras (also claimed for Corinth and Thesprotia); this one on the river Selleeis, location disputed since antiquity (Strabo 8.3.5, 7.7.9); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Selleeis (river, by Ephyra)
places.note: River Strabo could not securely place; a namesake Selleeis also flows past Arisbe in the Troad half of this Catalogue.
places.tradition: River by the Ephyra of Tlepolemus's mother's capture, unlocated, distinct from the Troad river of the same name (Strabo 8.3.5); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Syme
places.note: Small Dodecanese island between Rhodes and the Carian coast; Nireus's kingdom, modern Symi.

places.name: Nisyros
places.note: Volcanic Dodecanese island; modern Nisyros preserves the ancient name.

places.name: Carpathus
places.note: Large Dodecanese island between Rhodes and Crete; modern Karpathos preserves the ancient name (Homeric Crapathus).

places.name: Casus
places.note: Small island south of Carpathos; modern Kasos preserves the ancient name.

places.name: Cos
places.note: Dodecanese island, Eurypylus's kingdom before the Catalogue's own Cos-contingent leaders; modern Kos.

places.name: Calydnae Islands
places.note: Small island group near Cos; Strabo and later tradition identify them chiefly with Kalymnos.
places.tradition: Islets near Cos, identified with modern Kalymnos and the smaller Leros group (Strabo 10.5.19)

places.name: Pelasgian Argos
places.note: Homonym of Peloponnesian Argos; ancient tradition places this 'Pelasgian Argos' in the Thessalian plain, Achilles's realm.
places.tradition: Identified with the plain of Thessaly (not the Peloponnesian Argos of the same name), per ancient scholiasts and Strabo 9.5.6

places.name: Alus
places.note: Achaea Phthiotis town near the Malian Gulf; site associated with modern Almyros/Halos.
places.tradition: Thessalian coastal town near modern Almyros, on the Malian Gulf road (Strabo 9.5.8)

places.name: Alope
places.note: Small Achaea Phthiotis town grouped with Alus and Trachis; unlocated precisely.
places.tradition: Achaea Phthiotis, near Alus, exact site unknown (Strabo 9.5.8); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Trachis
places.note: Town below Oeta later refounded as Spartan-colonized Heraclea Trachinia; site near modern Ypati.
places.tradition: Near modern Ypati at the foot of Mt Oeta, associated with Heraclea Trachinia (Strabo 9.4.13-17)

places.name: Hellas
places.note: Homer's original, narrow 'Hellas': a district of Achaea Phthiotis, not yet the whole Greek world.

places.name: Phylace
places.note: Protesilaus's city in Achaea Phthiotis; Strabo places it in the same coastal district as Phthiotic Thebes.
places.tradition: Achaea Phthiotis, near modern Nea Anchialos/Phthiotic Thebes (Strabo 9.5.8)

places.name: Pyrasus
places.note: Coastal town with a precinct of Demeter; later absorbed into/near Phthiotic Thebes per Strabo.
places.tradition: Site of a Demeter sanctuary, near modern Nea Anchialos, Achaea Phthiotis (Strabo 9.5.14)

places.name: Iton
places.note: "Mother of flocks": site of the Thessalian federal sanctuary of Athena Itonia.
places.tradition: Site of the federal Thessalian sanctuary of Athena Itonia, near modern Philia (Strabo 9.5.14)

places.name: Antron
places.note: Coastal Achaea Phthiotis town facing Euboea across the strait; approximate site near modern Glypha.
places.tradition: Achaea Phthiotis coast opposite Euboea, near modern Glypha (Strabo 9.5.14)

places.name: Pteleos (Thessaly)
places.note: Thessalian coastal town whose name modern Pteleos village preserves; homonymous with a Messenian town in this Catalogue.
places.tradition: Achaea Phthiotis coast near modern Pteleos village, homonymous with the Messenian Pteleos (Strabo 9.5.14)

places.name: Pherae
places.note: Major Thessalian city on Lake Boebeis, later home of the tyrant Jason of Pherae; near modern Velestino.

places.name: Lake Boebeis
places.note: Thessalian lake by Pherae; the modern (much reduced) Lake Karla/Boibeis.

places.name: Boebe
places.note: Small Thessalian town giving the nearby lake its name; precise site unconfirmed.
places.tradition: Thessaly, on Lake Boebeis, exact site unknown; Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Glaphyrae
places.note: Minor Thessalian town in Eumelus's territory near Pherae and Iolcus; unlocated precisely.
places.tradition: Thessaly, near Pherae, exact site unknown; Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Iolcus
places.note: Jason and the Argonauts' port city; excavated Bronze Age site near modern Volos.

places.name: Methone (Thessaly)
places.note: Magnesian coastal town in Philoctetes's realm; homonymous with an unrelated Methone in Messenia.
places.tradition: Magnesian coast of Thessaly, near modern Nea Agchialos/Volos area, homonymous with Messenian Methone (Strabo 9.5.18)

places.name: Thaumacia
places.note: Small Magnesian coastal town in Philoctetes's realm; no confirmed modern site.
places.tradition: Magnesian coast of Thessaly, exact site unknown; Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Meliboea
places.note: Magnesian coastal town famed later for a purple dye; modern Melivoia village preserves the name.
places.tradition: Magnesian coast of Thessaly near modern Kato Ollympos/Melivoia (Strabo 9.5.15)

places.name: Olizon
places.note: Southern Magnesian coastal town in Philoctetes's realm; approximate site near modern Milina.
places.tradition: Southern tip of the Magnesian peninsula, Thessaly, near modern Milina (Strabo 9.5.15)

places.name: Tricca
places.note: Thessalian city with the oldest sanctuary of Asclepius in Greek tradition; modern Trikala occupies the site.

places.name: Ithome (Thessaly)
places.note: "Craggy" Thessalian town near Tricca, homonymous with the far better-known Messenian Ithome; unlocated precisely.
places.tradition: West Thessaly near Tricca, 'craggy,' exact site unknown, distinct from the famous Messenian Ithome; Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Ormenium
places.note: Thessalian town at the foot of Pelion in Eurypylus's realm; Strabo places it near the Magnesian border.
places.tradition: Thessaly/Magnesia border, near modern Ormenio or the foot of Mt Pelion (Strabo 9.5.18)

places.name: Spring Hypereia
places.note: Named spring Strabo locates in the middle of Pherae itself, not a separate town.
places.tradition: Spring at Pherae, Thessaly, per Strabo 9.5.18

places.name: Asterium
places.note: Thessalian town Strabo pairs with the white-peaked Titanus; unlocated precisely.
places.tradition: Thessaly, near Mt Titanus, exact site unknown (Strabo 9.5.18); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Titanus
places.note: "White-peaked" hill Strabo describes as a mass of white earth near Asterium; unlocated precisely.
places.tradition: Thessaly, a hill of white chalky earth near Asterium (Strabo 9.5.18); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Argissa
places.note: Lapith town on the Peneius near later Larissa; Strabo notes some identified it with Argura.
places.tradition: On the Peneius, near modern Larissa, Thessaly, sometimes identified with Argura (Strabo 9.5.19)

places.name: Gyrton
places.note: Lapith city in northeast Thessaly, associated in tradition with Peirithous's family.
places.tradition: Northeast Thessaly near modern Aghia, home of the Perrhaebian/Lapith Peirithous line (Strabo 9.5.19)

places.name: Orthe
places.note: Thessalian town Strabo tentatively equates with the citadel of Phalanna; unconfirmed.
places.tradition: Thessaly, possibly the acropolis of Phalanna per Strabo 9.5.19; Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Elone
places.note: Thessalian town Strabo says was later called Leimone; precise original site unconfirmed.
places.tradition: Thessaly, later renamed Leimone per Strabo 9.5.19; Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Oloosson
places.note: "White" Thessalian town in Perrhaebian territory; located near modern Elassona.
places.tradition: Northwest Thessaly near modern Elassona (Strabo 9.5.19)

places.name: Mount Pelion
places.note: Wooded mountain of the Magnesian peninsula, Thessaly, home of Chiron in myth; modern Pilio.

places.name: Aethices
places.note: Mountain people on Thessaly's western fringe, near the Perrhaebians and Pindus; territory only vaguely fixed.
places.tradition: A people/district on the western Thessalian-Epirote border, near Mt Pindus, exact bounds unknown (Strabo 9.5.11); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Cyphus
places.note: Gouneus's home town in Perrhaebian territory; Strabo does not fix a precise site.
places.tradition: Northwest Thessaly/Perrhaebia, exact site unknown (Strabo 9.5.19); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Titaressus (river)
places.note: River said to flow atop the Peneius without mixing, as an offshoot of the Styx; identified with the modern Xerias.
places.tradition: Tributary of the Peneius in northwest Thessaly, identified with the modern Xerias/Titarisios (Strabo 9.5.19-20)

places.name: Peneius (river)
places.note: Principal river of Thessaly, running through the Vale of Tempe; the modern Pineios.

places.name: Styx
places.note: River of the underworld by which the gods swear their most solemn oath; ancient tradition placed its earthly outlet at Nonacris in Arcadia.
places.tradition: Localized in antiquity at the waterfall of Nonacris, Arcadia, called Mavroneri (Herodotus 6.74; Paus. 8.17.6-18.6)

places.name: Magnesia (Thessaly)
places.note: Coastal district comprising the Pelion peninsula and lower Peneius valley, Thessaly; Prothous's contingent.

places.name: Aesepus (river)
places.note: River of the northern Troad flowing from Ida past Zeleia; the modern Gönen Çayı.

places.name: Adrasteia
places.note: Troad-Propontis town giving its name to the plain of Adrasteia and, later, to the epithet of Nemesis/Adrasteia.
places.tradition: Plain and town near modern Karacabey/Erdek area, southern Propontis coast (Strabo 13.1.13)

places.name: Apaesus
places.note: Small Propontis-coast town Strabo says was later called Paesus; precise site unconfirmed.
places.tradition: Propontis coast near Adrasteia, later renamed Paesus/Apaesus, exact site unknown (Strabo 13.1.19); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Pityeia
places.note: "Pine" town on the Propontis coast; Strabo connects the district with later Lampsacus.
places.tradition: Propontis coast, later identified with Lampsacus's territory (Strabo 13.1.19); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Mount Tereia
places.note: Hill-landmark Strabo places between Lampsacus and Zeleia; precise peak unidentified.
places.tradition: A hill on the Propontis coast between Lampsacus and Zeleia (Strabo 13.1.19); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Percote
places.note: Propontis coastal town between Abydos and Lampsacus in Asius's realm.
places.tradition: Propontis coast near modern Umurbey/Bergaz, between Abydos and Lampsacus (Strabo 13.1.19)

places.name: Practius (river)
places.note: River Strabo places between Percote and Abydos; also the name of a nearby town in later sources.
places.tradition: Small stream between Percote and Abydos, Propontis coast (Strabo 13.1.19-21)

places.name: Arisbe
places.note: Asius's home city on the Propontis coast, colonized in tradition from Mytilene.
places.tradition: Propontis coast near modern Musaköy, between Abydos and Lampsacus (Strabo 13.1.21)

places.name: Selleeis (river, Troad)
places.note: River by Arisbe from which Asius's horses come; a second, unrelated Homeric river Selleeis is named for Rhodes's Ephyra.
places.tradition: Stream by Arisbe in the Troad, unlocated precisely, distinct from the river of the same name near Rhodian Ephyra; Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Larisa (Troad)
places.note: Pelasgian city, homonymous with the Thessalian Larisa; Strabo records several rival candidate sites near the Troad/Aeolis coast.
places.tradition: Aeolis/Troad, exact site disputed since antiquity; candidates include a site near Cyme (Strabo 13.3.2-3, 13.1.70); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Thrace
places.note: Region north of the Hellespont and Propontis; homeland of Acamas's and Peirous's contingent.

places.name: Land of the Cicones
places.note: Thracian coastal people allied to Troy here; the same Cicones whose city Ismarus Odysseus later sacks.
places.tradition: Aegean-Thracian coast around modern Maroneia, homeland of the Ciconian allies (Strabo 7 fr. 44)

places.name: Paeonia
places.note: Region on the Axius river, north of Macedon; Pyraechmes leads its Trojan-allied archers.
places.tradition: Region along the middle Axius valley, north of Macedonia (Strabo 7 fr. 4, 11)

places.name: Amydon
places.note: Paeonian city on the Axius, already legendary/vanished by the time of later Greek geography.
places.tradition: Paeonia, on the lower Axius, said destroyed before historical times (Strabo 12.3.20, fr.); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Axius (river)
places.note: Major Macedonian river reaching the Thermaic Gulf; the modern Vardar.

places.name: Paphlagonia
places.note: Black Sea coastal region of north-central Anatolia; Pylaemenes leads its Trojan-allied contingent.

places.name: Eneti
places.note: People whose homeland the Romans later linked to the Italian Veneti; Strabo could not fix their Paphlagonian location precisely.
places.tradition: Paphlagonian coast, origin-point of the later Veneti migration legend, exact location disputed since antiquity (Strabo 12.3.8, 12.3.25)

places.name: Cytorus
places.note: Paphlagonian coastal town famed for boxwood; near modern Gideros on the Turkish Black Sea coast.
places.tradition: Black Sea coast near modern Gideros/Kidros, Paphlagonia (Strabo 12.3.10)

places.name: Sesamus
places.note: Paphlagonian coastal town later refounded as Amastris; near modern Amasra, Turkey.
places.tradition: Black Sea coast near modern Amasra, Paphlagonia, later called Amastris (Strabo 12.3.10)

places.name: Parthenius (river)
places.note: Paphlagonian coastal river; the modern Bartın Çayı.

places.name: Cromna
places.note: Paphlagonian coastal town Strabo groups with Cytorus and Sesamus without a precise site.
places.tradition: Paphlagonian coast, exact site unknown, near Cytorus and Sesamus (Strabo 12.3.10); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Aegialus (Paphlagonia)
places.note: "The coastland" of Paphlagonia; a generic descriptive name shared with the Achaean-side Aegialus (Il. 2.575).
places.tradition: Paphlagonian coast, 'the shoreland,' homonymous with the Achaean Aegialus in this Catalogue; Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Erythini
places.note: "Red" coastal cliffs of Paphlagonia named as a landmark; no confirmed modern site.
places.tradition: Paphlagonian coast, 'the red cliffs,' exact site unknown (Strabo 12.3.10); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Halizones
places.note: One of the most disputed Catalogue peoples; Strabo surveys and rejects several rival ancient theories of their location.
places.tradition: Location disputed since antiquity: candidates range from inland Anatolia to the Black Sea coast (Strabo 12.3.20-27 devotes an extended digression to the dispute); Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Alybe
places.note: Named only for its silver; ancient scholarship already treated its location as an open, much-debated problem.
places.tradition: "Birthplace of silver": among the most famously unlocated Homeric place-names, disputed since antiquity (Strabo 12.3.20-27)

places.name: Mysia
places.note: Region of northwest Anatolia south of the Troad and Propontis; Chromis and Ennomus lead its contingent.

places.name: Phrygia
places.note: Central Anatolian region; Phorcys and Ascanius lead its Trojan-allied contingent.

places.name: Ascania (Phrygia)
places.note: District named for a lake in northwest Phrygia/Bithynia, generally identified with modern Lake İznik.
places.tradition: Region around Lake Ascania in northwest Phrygia, modern Lake İznik (Strabo 12.4.5, 14.5.29)

places.name: Maeonia
places.note: Region of west Anatolia later called Lydia; Mesthles and Antiphus lead its contingent.

places.name: Lake Gygaea
places.note: Lake in Maeonia/Lydia below Mt Tmolus; identified with the modern Marmara Gölü.

places.name: Mount Tmolus
places.note: Mountain of Maeonia/Lydia overlooking Sardis; the modern Bozdağ range.

places.name: Caria
places.note: Region of southwest Anatolia; Nastes and Amphimachus lead its 'foreign-speaking' contingent.

places.name: Miletus (Anatolia)
places.note: Major Ionian/Carian coastal city, homonymous with the Cretan Miletus named earlier in this Catalogue.

places.name: Mount Phthires
places.note: "Louse mountain," a landmark near Carian Miletus; no confirmed identification with a modern peak.
places.tradition: Caria, near Miletus and the Maeander, exact peak unidentified; Simpson–Lazenby, The Catalogue of the Ships in Homer's Iliad (1970)

places.name: Maeander (river)
places.note: Anatolian river proverbial for its winding course, reaching the sea near Miletus; the modern Büyük Menderes.

places.name: Mount Mycale
places.note: Coastal mountain of Ionia opposite Samos, site of the 479 BC battle; the modern Dilek Dağı.

places.name: Lycia
places.note: Region of southwest Anatolia; Sarpedon and Glaucus lead its distant Trojan-allied contingent.

places.name: Xanthus (river, Lycia)
places.note: Chief river of Lycia, distinct from the Trojan river Scamander/Xanthus named elsewhere in the epic; the modern Eşen Çayı.

places.name: Sounion
places.note: The 'sacred cape of the Athenians' (Od. 3.278) at the southern tip of Attica, where Menelaus's helmsman Phrontis died at the tiller and was buried, delaying the fleet. The Poseidon temple whose ruins stand there today is later (5th c. BC) than the epic setting, but the headland is the same real cape (Pleiades 580108).

places.name: Lesbos
places.note: Large island off the Aeolian coast of Asia Minor where Nestor's and Menelaus's homebound squadrons debated the safer sea-route to Euboea (Od. 3.169-175) before striking out across open water for Geraistos. Coordinate is a representative point on the island, not a single settlement.

places.name: Geraistos
places.note: Harbor/cape at the southern tip of Euboea (modern Porto Kastri) where Nestor's and Menelaus's ships made landfall after the open-sea crossing from near Chios/Lesbos, sacrificing to Poseidon for the safe passage (Od. 3.177-179).

places.name: Pherae
places.tradition: Identified since antiquity with the settlement near modern Kalamata, Messenia (Pausanias 4.30.2, who explicitly glosses Od. 3.488's 'house of Diocles' as 'the city of Pherae in Messene'); distinct from the better-known Thessalian Pherae (home of Admetus).
places.note: Home of Diocles son of Ortilochus, where Telemachus and Peisistratus break their overland journey from Pylos to Sparta, spending the night before pressing on the next day (Od. 3.488-497).

places.name: Erembi
places.tradition: Unresolved since antiquity: Strabo (1.2.34), reporting Poseidonius, favors identifying the Erembi with the Arabians (on a conjectured textual/etymological link), while noting a rival ancient view that Homer means the Troglodytae; no consensus location exists, ancient or modern.
places.note: People named in Menelaus's summary list of the lands he wandered through before reaching home (Od. 4.83-85), alongside Cyprus, Phoenicia, Egypt, the Ethiopians, the Sidonians, and Libya. No fixed site: not pinned on the map (CLAUDE.md apparatus honesty).
